notes: Read on Fujifilm's US healthcare product site (healthcaresolutions-us.fujifilm.com) as instructed, not the corporate fujifilm.com home; the page-candidates home field pointed at a third-party page and was ignored. Seven pages read, all HTTP 200 and not thin. 'Synapse' and 'Fujifilm Healthcare' are the vendor's index aliases, so bare 'Synapse PACS' mentions were treated as name mentions; Synapse RIS, Synapse EIS, Synapse Enterprise PACS (including the shorthand 'Synapse Enterprise'), Synapse 7x and Synapse Universal Viewer were coded as module names. C08 groups 'cloud-enabled', 'cloud deployment options' and one 'cloud-native' line as cloud availability; Fujifilm's pages say cloud-enabled and cloud-based hosting, not cloud-native, which a reviewer may want split out. C11 rests on the Synapse Mobility zero-footprint, browser-neutral client and the zero-download PACS viewer; Fujifilm also describes Synapse VX as an elective native application. The 'Synapse 5 and newer versions added server-side rendering' line, data-portability and exit-cost lines, KLAS scores and module coverage lists were treated as capability descriptions, ratings or comparisons. No claim is wrong or stale, so no cited page was read for causes. Pass 2 (8 Oct 2026): no browser read exists for Fujifilm and no page was blocked or thin, so nothing was re-classed; C05 stays unverifiable after re-checking all seven snapshots (only 'one universal diagnostic viewer' appears). The 17 gap lines are best-for, reliability, KLAS or capability lines, or a general cloud-or-on-premise remark not about Fujifilm, all out of scope. The comparison tables carry only Synapse module names and cloud, on-premises, hybrid or web-viewing cells already coded under C01 to C04 and C08 to C11, plus KLAS scores, so no claim or instance was added. No claim is wrong or stale, so the consistency check changed nothing.
